objective: QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel::NONE>::decode_vector is bottlenecked by a scalar, branch-per-lane software FP16->FP32 conversion loop: it inlines decode_fp16 (fp16-inl.h) as integer bit-decode that per element loads the FP16 halfword (lhu 0x389672), isolates exponent/sign with shifts and ANDs, branches on the zero/subnormal and inf/nan special cases (including the fmv.w.x/fsub.s/fmv.x.w float round-trip at 0x389658-0x389666), ORs the sign, and stores FP32 (sw 0x38969e); all three sampled addresses are inside this body, while the build ISA (v1p0+zvfhmin, zvl128b) provides the RVV widening conversion vfwcvt.f.f.v that the loop omits.

changes.rationale: Add an RVV fast path to QuantizerFP16 decode_vector gated on __riscv_v && __riscv_zvfhmin: per iteration vsetvl_e16m* on remaining count, vle16 load of FP16 codes, vfwcvt.f.f.v widening FP16->FP32 (native IEEE handling of normals, denormals, ±0, ±Inf, NaN), vse32 store, with tail handling for d % VL and the existing scalar decode_fp16 loop retained as the fallback; add a masked/narrow repair only if bit-exact NaN-payload/sNaN parity with decode_fp16 is required.
instructions: Runtime exposes v + zvfhmin (build ISA already tags v1p0+zvfhmin, zvl128b; verify via /proc/cpuinfo or hwprobe before relying on the tag).
decode_vector must remain bit-identical to the scalar decode_fp16 reference for every FP16 bit pattern the consumer can produce.
d is large enough to amortize one vsetvl and vector load/store per vector (benchmark QT_fp16 uses code_size=256 bytes, i.e. d=128; worst realistic d for this template is the quantizer's d).
